Its slim stem (spear) is edible, and is used as vegetable in Taiwan, mostly produced at Meinong District, Kaohsiung.

When conducting surveys or experiments with large populations where it's impractical to collect data from every member individually, various statistical techniques can help select representative subsamples. In some cases, such as when there are natural groupings within your population or you want to ensure certain characteristics are present in your study, using either stratified sampling or cluster sampling may be a better choice than simply selecting individuals randomly through straightforward procedures like simple random sampling.

The relationship between these approaches lies primarily on their ability to provide reliable insights into larger groups by carefully choosing smaller portions of them. A key characteristic shared among many valid research designs involves ensuring unbiased estimates derived from sampled information; this often necessitates employing "equal-probability" sampling schemes. These types of sampling strategies guarantee that each element under consideration possesses identical chances of getting chosen during the process—a concept known as EPSM ("Equal Probability Sampling Mechanism"). While Simple Random Sample (SRS), i.e., picking elements completely at random without regard to order or position, inherently adheres to this principle, several alternative mechanisms do so too despite deviating structurally from traditional forms of pure randomness. Examples include Multistage Samples and Systematic Random Samplers. However, unlike SRS, they don’t necessarily make sure that distinct combinations drawn hold equivalent likelihoods - something crucial for maintaining absolute impartiality in selections made via true SRS processes. The end result though remains Epsems – instances wherein constituent parts enjoy uniform odds of participation regardless of how complex the underlying mechanism driving those choices turns out to be. Such arrangements naturally lend themselves towards 'self-weighted' scenarios because then the reciprocal values associated with respective entities' initial possibilities get evenly distributed across the entire pool.

Unlike the first film, it is not based on any existing book, and has no relation to the second installment in the book series, The Princess Diaries, Volume II: Princess in the Spotlight. In the film, Mia Thermopolis learns that before she can succeed her grandmother as queen of Genovia, she must marry or else relinquish the throne.
Most of the cast returned from the first film, including Anne Hathaway, Julie Andrews, Héctor Elizondo, Heather Matarazzo, and Larry Miller. Garry Marshall returned to direct and Debra Martin Chase and Whitney Houston to produce. New characters include Viscount Mabrey (John Rhys-Davies), Lord Nicholas Devereaux (Chris Pine, in his feature film debut), and Andrew Jacoby (Callum Blue).
The film grossed $135.3 million worldwide but received mixed to unfavorable reviews from critics. As of 2024 a sequel is in development, with Adele Lim attached as director.
